DataCenters.title: Data center feasibility and construction
DataCenters.description: We assess the feasibility of your next data center and coordinate design, construction and commissioning with specialists.
DataCenters.workIntro: Before defining the build, we compare what the operation needs with what the site can support.
DataCenters.siteDetail: We review the available space, electrical capacity and room for future expansion.
DataCenters.systemsDetail: With the specialists, we assess how network links will reach the site and how the facility will remove heat from the equipment.
DataCenters.deliveryDetail: We sequence the work, coordinate the specialists involved and support the facility through commissioning.
DataCenters.output: A phased plan and a preliminary budget.
DataCenters.imageAlt: A server aisle lined with equipment racks and orange fiber cables.

sequra.what: seQura provides checkout financing for merchants across southern Europe.
sequra.did: We built AI agents to support merchant onboarding, from the moment a business joins seQura until it can offer financing at checkout.

scuticchio.what: Scuticchio is a Buenos Aires production company specializing in sound, lighting, video and streaming.
scuticchio.did: We replaced its operations system and migrated the records for over 9,500 events. The team prepares bilingual quotes and scans QR codes to identify individual pieces of equipment.

legalwise.what: Legalwise Seminars provides continuing professional development for lawyers in Australia.
legalwise.did: We designed and built a portal for law firms. Learning managers can allocate training hours to lawyers, track their progress and collect certificates for firm-wide reporting.

alveo.what: Alveo manufactures road signage and molded plastic products in Mexico City.
alveo.did: We worked with the team to turn an AI application built for Alveo into products that other road infrastructure companies can use.

seeds.what: Seeds connects companies with independent professionals across Latin America and the United States.
seeds.did: We connected its CRM, an operations dashboard and an assistant that searches internal knowledge. The team can look up information and automate follow-up tasks using its own data.

martis.what: Marti’s ships auto parts from Miami directly to customers in Argentina.
martis.did: We built a storefront that matches 2,958 parts against more than 21,000 vehicle compatibility records. Buyers find the right part and see the final price in pesos. Staff manage the catalog, pricing and orders in the same system.

areafit.what: AreaFit runs a network of gyms in Spain.
areafit.did: We built the dashboard for Fiti, its WhatsApp and Instagram assistant. The team can read conversations by location, identify common questions and see how customers rate the support they receive.

psima.what: Psi Mammoliti provides online therapy to Spanish-speaking patients worldwide.
psima.did: We built and operate the system that connects patients, therapists, payments and reconciliation. It also brings together WhatsApp follow-ups and the metrics the team uses every day.

elliecare.what: Ellie Care develops technology for older adults and their families.
elliecare.did: We built a system that turns family photographs and a written memory into a narrated film. AI writes the story, generates the voiceover, animates the images and delivers the video.

ulc.what: ULC works with importers and exporters in Argentina.
ulc.did: We built a CRM that finds companies by the goods they import or export. It uses customs records to identify prospects, adds contact details and ranks leads against the sales team’s target profile.

muecas.what: Muecas produces and distributes snack bars, chocolates and alfajores.
muecas.did: We built an assistant that answers questions using the company’s own documents, automated internal tasks and trained the team to maintain those workflows.

HowWeWork.label: Our FDE approach
HowWeWork.title: The engineers who listen
HowWeWork.intro: We call this forward deployed engineering. Our engineers work alongside the people who know the operation and stay involved once the system is in daily use.
HowWeWork.photoAlt: Pablo Loyúdice at the NoCoda studio.

steps.title: Follow a real case.
steps.description: We ask to see the last order, complaint or month-end close. The person who handled it walks us through each step, including the spreadsheet only their team knows about.

steps.title: Design with the people using it.
steps.description: We map how information travels, pinpoint the bottleneck and agree on what should change. The people who showed us the problem try the first version.

steps.title: Build the infrastructure.
steps.description: We connect existing tools, organise the data and define access. Applications, AI models and integrations share a foundation the team can operate.

steps.title: Stay involved in production.
steps.description: We work through the first weeks of use, monitor errors and adjust as new cases come in. The team learns to run the system and knows whom to call when things change.
